messages:
Amelia: Quick follow-up on the RFC about service auth / actor model — trying to reconcile project-scoped API keys with service-to-service JWTs. TL;DR: propose API keys are project-bound principals (longer lived, limited scope) and services use short-lived JWTs (minted via token-exchange) that can carry delegated project claims. Thoughts?

PJ: I like keeping human/operator API keys separate from service tokens. Avoid conflating attacker blast radius. Suggest: API keys = project-scoped, role-bound; service tokens = short-lived, with actor+project claims via token-exchange.

Samir: Agree in principle. One thing to call out: cross-project reads (billing/aggregators) — how do we allow a service to read across projects without giving overly broad org permissions?

Maria: We could introduce an org-level role like `cross_project_aggregator` which is allowed to request short-lived delegation into specific target projects using a constrained impersonation flow. That flow should record which projects were delegated and why.

Jordan: Auditability is critical. If we allow impersonation/delegation, every exchange must capture `original_principal`, `delegated_by`, `delegate_scope`, and a trace_id. That way logs can distinguish the true originator from the ephemeral principal. :thumbsup:

deploybot: Suggestion: enforce very short TTLs on exchanged JWTs. Example JWT payload we use in other flows:

```
{
  "iss": "https://auth.internal",
  "sub": "service:billing-svc",
  "actor": "service:ingest-svc",
  "project": "proj-42",
  "exp": 1710000300,
  "jti": "xyz-123",
  "delegated_by": "svc-account:billing-runner",
  "trace_id": "t-abc-987"
}
```

Amelia: Proposed enforcement model (sketch):
- API keys: long-lived creds bound to a user or service-account and a single project; limited role bindings (e.g., `project.viewer`, `project.deployer`). No API key may directly access org-scoped resources.
- Service-to-service: short-lived JWT from token-exchange with `actor` and `project` claims. Delegation requires `delegate` permission on the project and creates an immutable audit entry.
- RBAC precedence at check time: explicit resource bindings > project-level role > org-level role. If multiple apply, the most specific binding wins.

PJ: Edge-case: third-party integrators needing long-term access but can't run token-exchange. Maybe we define a `service_account_api_key` with stricter rotation and org-level approvals (and a billing/contract gate).

Samir: We should specify the token-exchange flow in the follow-up RFC: authn issues a short-lived session token (exp=5m), then the token-exchange endpoint mints the service JWT (exp=1m-5m) with delegated claims and writes an audit event.

Maria: Enforcement additions: disallow project-scoped API keys from reading org-only resources. Also add rate-limits per principal and per credential type.

Amelia: Questions for the RFC: 1) require explicit `delegate` permission for impersonation? 2) require audit log + trace_id for all exchanges? 3) add console warnings/lints for overly-broad API keys? My preference: yes to all.

Jordan: +1 to all. Also recommend adding an automated 'least-privilege' lint in the console that flags API keys with wildcard/project:* roles.

deploybot: noted — created infra/2345 to add token-exchange endpoint telemetry and audit hooks.

Amelia: Thanks — I'll draft the follow-up RFC with diagrams (token-exchange, audit flow, RBAC precedence) and some sample enforcement pseudocode. Will ping for review once posted. cc @PJ @Samir :eyes:
